Why AI visibility matters now: a growing share of people looking for a dance studio ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google's AI overview before they ever open a map. Studios that don't structure their site for those tools simply don't get mentioned — regardless of how good the studio actually is. In our checks, every studio the AI engines named was inside Houston itself — none of the three studios in Bellaire or West University Place came up.

13 studios compete for Houston's dance students. None has finished the work AI search now rewards.

We audited 13 dance and ballroom studios serving the Houston market head to head: site quality, Google's local results, and 6 live checks across ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI. The sites range from 44 to 87. The AI engines name only six of the 13, and all three studios in Bellaire and West University Place were never named once. The field averages 59 (D) on AI readiness, 12 of 13 have no FAQ or Q&A structured data, and 12 of 13 have no llms.txt file. Whichever studio closes that gap first changes the answer for everyone searching this market.

Prepared by SiteTradeIn · Market snapshot generated 3 Oct 2026 · Independent audit — not commissioned by any studio in the field · See the ranked list

About this report

This is a market-wide snapshot, not an audit of a single business. We picked one competitive local market — dance and ballroom instruction in the Houston, TX area — and ran the same measurement against every studio that competes for it: an automated site-quality grade across seven categories, where each studio shows up in Google's local results, and 6 live checks asking three AI engines who they'd recommend for two real buyer queries. Every studio named below is graded on identical criteria, on the same day, with no advance notice.

The point isn't to single any one studio out — it's to show what an AI-search-era competitive landscape actually looks like once you measure it instead of guessing at it. If your studio is one of the 13 below, this is where you stand today.

What the field shows

  • Premier Dance USA (87) and Dance With Me Houston (85) lead on site quality, and the field runs down to 44. Two scores are shared. Every one of the top five still carries at least one D or F category.
  • No studio earns an A for AI readiness. The field averages 59 (D) on the category that decides whether an AI engine can read, trust and quote a site; the best score in the market is 85.
  • 12 of 13 have no FAQ or Q&A structured data, and 12 of 13 have no llms.txt file — the two cheapest AI-answer signals available. No studio in the market has both.
  • All 13 studios have images without alt text, from 6 of 78 images to 332 of 670 — easy points every site in the field is leaving on the table.
  • Five of the 13 are franchise locations (one Dance With Me and four Fred Astaire); the rest are independent studios.
  • One site in the field still isn't served over HTTPS — a critical flag browsers show visitors before they see a single class schedule.
  • The gap between #1 and #13 is 43 points on identical criteria. Nothing in the scorecard requires a rebuild or a rebrand to close it — just the work.

For a studio not doing this work, that's the default outcome — not a penalty, just the result of nobody in that seat having claimed it yet.

What separates the winners from the rest

  • Off-site proof, not just on-site polish. In its two answers, Perplexity cited third-party review and listing sites (yelp.com). The studios named most are the ones those sources already describe clearly.
  • Being unmistakably “in Houston.” Every AI mention went to a studio inside the city. Studios that serve Houston from nearby towns need pages, profiles and listings that say so in the words people search.
  • A complete, specific site. The strongest sites have no missing H1s or meta descriptions, alt text on their images, and schema that describes what the studio actually is. No studio in this field has all of that yet.
  • Content matched to how people actually ask. The broad question and the ballroom question pull from different result sets — a studio needs to answer both.

Methodology & notes

Field (13 studios): premierdanceusa.com, dancewithmeusa.com/studio/houston-dance-studio, fredastaire.com/houston-heights, fredastaire.com/bellaire, fredastaire.com/west-university, omnisalsa.com, fredastaire.com/river-oaks, amayadance.com, innermestudios.com, danceez.com, riveroaksdancing.com, salsaeddy.com, thedancewhisperer.com. Chosen from live Google searches on 3 Oct 2026: every adult ballroom, Latin or partner-dance studio with a working website that appeared in Google's local results for Houston dance searches. Fred Astaire West University was added from the west Houston searches run for this split. Left out: Wedding Dance Houston (no studio address), dance halls and venues (Neon Boots, Rowdy's, Stampede, Sawyer Station), fitness, hip-hop and kids' studios (DivaDance, Soundbox, SoReal, The Dance Barre, Hunter Dance Center), clubs and line-dance groups, studios whose websites don't load (Dance Passion's site redirects to a broken security certificate, so it couldn't be audited), and studios in west Houston, Katy, The Woodlands, Spring, Cypress and Sugar Land, which belong to other Dance Booking Rank areas.

Site audit: the same SiteTradeIn engine run for every studio on 3 Oct 2026, up to six pages per site, seven categories. Franchise locations that live on a national website (Dance With Me, Fred Astaire) share that site's robots.txt, llms.txt, sitemap and templates.

AI visibility: 6 live checks — ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI, each asked “What are the best dance studios in Houston, TX?” and “What are the best ballroom dance studios in Houston, TX?” with a request for a top-five numbered list. Rankings are taken from each engine's own list; presence was confirmed by reading the raw response text, and every franchise mention was matched to its location. Each question was asked in a fresh session of each engine's public web app (ChatGPT and Perplexity logged out, Google's AI Mode), not through a developer API.

Google: local (Places) and first-page organic results captured in a live browser session on 3 Oct 2026 for “ballroom dance lessons houston tx”; “dance lessons houston tx”; “salsa lessons houston tx”; “wedding dance lessons houston tx”; “two step lessons houston tx”; “ballroom dance lessons west houston tx”, plus the organic searches “best dance studios in houston tx” and “ballroom dance studio houston”. Each query named the city; results vary by searcher location and over time.

Independence. This report is a market-wide measurement, not commissioned by or customized for any single studio named in it.

Limits. AI answers and search results vary between runs and over time; these are a point-in-time sample, not a fixed ranking.
